newsitem.title: GERMANY: German harvest moves along, weather outlook bright.
newsitem.headline: German harvest moves along, weather outlook bright.

text.p: Harvesting is gathering pace across Germany amid forecasts for dry and sunny weather next week, the meteorological office DWD said.
The barley harvest was complete in several regions and rye and rapeseed harvests had begun.
Spring grain and winter wheat crops need another fortnight before they can be harvested.
Maize and sugar beet benefited from localised showers this week which in some eastern German regions meant farmers had to spend money on drying barley and were unable to cut grass for silage.
Lower Saxony and Schleswig Holstein in the north also reported some problems with excessive moisture and lodging of barley, rapeseed, and triticale.
Rye falling numbers, which measure baking quality, were down in Lower Saxony, the local farm union reported.
But rainfall next week should be confined to small areas in the south and east while maximum temperatures of up to 27 degrees were forecast for the period up to August 6.
